title: Compass: Model Sourcing & Lifecycle Trigger Specification
creator: Priya Nair
description: Define a repeatable specification (the "Compass") for sourcing and lifecycle triggers for model variants used by Enterprise customers. The spec will standardize thresholds, signals, and playbooks that move a model from evaluation -> pilot -> production -> deprecation, and identify procurement triggers (e.g., outage, price delta, latency regression). Outputs: sourcing rubric, trigger matrix, pilot checklist, and a lightweight scoring dashboard for Sales/SEs.
acceptance_criteria: A clear sourcing rubric documented: cost, latency, accuracy, quantization maturity, legal/regional constraints
Trigger matrix covering 8+ signals with concrete numeric thresholds and mitigation playbooks
Pilot checklist with required bench results, data-security approvals, and SLA/contract templates
Prototype scoring dashboard (spreadsheet + Grafana links) that produces a per-model "enterprise readiness" score
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales Ops, Legal, and Runtime Engineering
tasks: Interview 6 enterprise AE/SEs to capture purchase blockers and fallback tolerances (owner: Marco)
Run benchmark suite for 6 candidate models across 3 seq-lens to estimate cost/latency/quality delta (owner: ENG bench team)
Draft sourcing rubric and weightings, circulate to Sales Ops and Product for feedback
Prototype scoring sheet and wire up Grafana panel for live fallback signals
Align with Legal on regional compliance flags and required contract clauses
Create Pilot readiness checklist and template PRD for trials

decisions_and_tradeoffs: Weighted-sum scoring chosen over classifier for interpretability by Sales; tradeoff: more manual weight tuning required
Thresholds will be intentionally conservative for first pilots (favor reliability over marginal cost savings), with plan to relax after 2 successful pilots

We will require quantization compatibility checks for Dedicated/Dedicated-reserved SKUs but allow hosted fallback variants for Hosted customers — tradeoff introduces extra routing complexity handled by Runtime team
risks: Bench results may not reflect real customer prompts (mitigation: include 3 customer promptsets in pilot)
Legal/reg requirements could prevent rapid provisioning in certain regions (mitigation: maintain catalog of compliant model mirrors)
Score volatility when models are updated frequently by third-party vendors (mitigation: add model-change delta signal into trigger matrix)
